notes: OpenAI-compatible: standard `chat/completions`, OpenAI-style SSE chunks + [DONE], OpenAI function-tool schema.

Catalog resells other labs' models under Venice-hosted ids (claude-sonnet-5, claude-fable-5, openai-gpt-52, openai-gpt-52-codex, gemini-3-5-flash) alongside Venice's own open-weight lineup -- a Venice-only key still gets multi-family routing, and these ids intentionally collide with the native anthropic/openai/gemini manifests (see verification.capabilities and router.go Rule 3 bare-id resolution).

Capability flags (tools/vision) below are TRAINING-KNOWLEDGE pending first-party confirmation -- the dynamic /models endpoint (which would confirm them) is unreachable from this build environment. Prices are first-party (see verification.pricing). context/max_output are intentionally omitted (not just null) for every model: unset, they read as unverified fail-closed exactly like a model absent from the catalog would.

streaming_usage is intentionally NOT declared for any model: Venice's OpenAI-compat semantics (stream_options.include_usage honored) are plausible but unconfirmed first-party, so a request that REQUIRES streaming usage will not auto-route to a Venice model until this is confirmed -- an honest gap, not a bug.

verification.shape_source: OpenAI-compatible API (api.venice.ai/api/v1); Bearer auth, standard chat/completions shape
verification.pricing_note: Model ids and USD/1M-token input/output prices below were fetched verbatim from Venice's own docs mirror (github.com/veniceai/api-docs, overview/pricing.mdx) on 2026-07-05. Not backfilled from training-data memory.
verification.capabilities_note: tools:true is set only on models where function-calling is well-established on Venice per training knowledge; it is NOT first-party confirmed (the dynamic models endpoint that would confirm capability flags is unreachable from this environment). context/max_output are omitted outright rather than guessed.

models.notes: Claude Sonnet 5 resold via Venice. Id collides with anthropic's native claude-sonnet-5 -- see router.go Rule 3 bare-id resolution (first enabled+non-tripped provider that owns the id wins, in provider registration order; not a hardcoded native-over-resale preference).
Claude Fable 5 resold via Venice. Id collides with anthropic's native claude-fable-5 -- see router.go Rule 3 bare-id resolution.
Id collides with the gemini manifest's gemini ids only in family naming, not literally (gemini.json ships gemini-2.5-pro/gemini-2.5-flash, distinct ids) -- no Rule 3 collision for this one.
